newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN pulls out staff from east Zaire refugee area.
newsitem.headline: UN pulls out staff from east Zaire refugee area.

text.p: United Nations and aid agency staff pulled out of eastern Zaire's biggest refugee area on Friday after the Zairean army ordered them to leave, a U.N. refugee agency spokesman said.

Fernando del Mundo said aid workers in Tingi-Tingi region, host to some 170,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees, were told to leave by midday on Friday. Aid agency staff maintain no overnight presence in the remote area but fly in and out every day.
The pullout order followed reports from the region that rebels fighting Zairean troops seized the strategic eastern town of Kindu, some 250 km (160 miles) south of Tingi-Tingi.

Rwandan Hutu refugees told UNHCR and aid workers before they left that they too had been ordered by the Zairean army to move by midday on Friday, del Mundo said, but he said his agency had no way of knowing where they were by the end of the day.
Kindu, a heavily-fortified transport hub on the Zaire River, had the northernmost working station on a rail line to South Africa. It also had a large airport used by the military.
Aid workers said Zairean troop reinforcements and mercenaries arrived at Tingi-Tingi on Friday from the city of Kisangani, backed by warplanes and helicopter gunships.

The rebels have seized a stretch of eastern Zaire more than 1,000 km (600 miles) long since October. Zaire accuses Rwanda, Uganda and Burundi of sending troops to fight alongside the rebels but all three countries denied involvement.
